subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 34-year-old woman presents with episodic palpitations, diaphoresis, and pounding headaches. CT shows a 4-cm left adrenal mass, and plasma metanephrines are markedly elevated. The surgeon explains that the tumor arises from chromaffin cells that receive direct neural input.
question: Which of the following best describes the innervation of the adrenal medulla?

options.text: Preganglionic sympathetic fibers release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors on chromaffin cells
Postganglionic sympathetic fibers release norepinephrine onto alpha-1 adrenergic receptors on chromaffin cells
Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors on chromaffin cells
Postganglionic parasympathetic fibers release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors on chromaffin cells
Somatic motor neurons release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors at a peripheral ganglion

explanation_correct: The adrenal medulla is directly innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers. These fibers release acetylcholine onto nicotinic (NN) receptors on chromaffin cells, triggering release of epinephrine into the bloodstream. Unlike all other sympathetic targets, no postganglionic neuron is involved, which is why catecholamine release is a classic 'blood-borne' (hormonal) transmission. This anatomy explains catecholamine excess states such as pheochromocytoma.

explanation_incorrect.B: Postganglionic sympathetic fibers release norepinephrine onto alpha-1 and beta receptors on effector tissues such as vascular smooth muscle, not onto the adrenal medulla; the medulla skips the postganglionic neuron entirely.
explanation_incorrect.C: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers (cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X and pelvic splanchnic nerves) supply ganglia of the parasympathetic division, not the adrenal medulla.
explanation_incorrect.D: Postganglionic parasympathetic fibers release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors on targets such as cardiac muscle, smooth muscle, and exocrine glands, not on adrenal chromaffin cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Somatic motor neurons synapse directly at the neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle using nicotinic (NM) receptors; they do not synapse in ganglia and do not supply the adrenal medulla.

educationalObjective: Recall that the adrenal medulla is directly innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers releasing acetylcholine on nicotinic receptors.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 22-year-old college student develops drenching palm and axillary sweat while studying for final examinations, even without heat or exercise. Her physician notes that eccrine sweat glands are unusual among sympathetic effector tissues with respect to their neurotransmitter.
question: Which of the following best describes the autonomic innervation of eccrine sweat glands?

options.text: Postganglionic sympathetic fibers release norepinephrine acting on beta-2 receptors
Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers release acetylcholine acting on muscarinic receptors
Postganglionic sympathetic fibers release acetylcholine acting on muscarinic receptors
Somatic motor fibers release acetylcholine acting on nicotinic receptors
Preganglionic sympathetic fibers release norepinephrine acting on alpha-1 receptors

explanation_correct: Sweat glands are part of the sympathetic pathway, but their postganglionic fibers are the exception to the noradrenergic rule: they release acetylcholine, which acts on muscarinic receptors (M receptors, including M3). First Aid summarizes this as the sympathetic nervous system producing a 'chold' (cholinergic) sweat. Emotionally induced sweating during an examination illustrates this cholinergic sympathetic pathway.

explanation_incorrect.A: Most postganglionic sympathetic fibers do release norepinephrine, but sweat glands are the classic exception; beta-2 receptors mediate effects such as bronchodilation and vasodilation, not sweating.
explanation_incorrect.B: The parasympathetic division does not supply sweat glands; sweating is a sympathetic function even though the final transmitter is acetylcholine.
explanation_incorrect.D: Somatic motor fibers release acetylcholine on nicotinic (NM) receptors only at the neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle, not on sweat glands.
explanation_incorrect.E: Preganglionic fibers of both autonomic divisions are cholinergic; norepinephrine is released by postganglionic sympathetic fibers (except sweat glands).

educationalObjective: Remember that sympathetic sweat gland innervation is cholinergic (postganglionic ACh on muscarinic receptors), producing a 'chold' sweat.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A neuroscience researcher is tracing autonomic pathways in a cadaver dissection. She identifies a neuron whose cell body lies in the sympathetic chain ganglion and whose axon travels a long distance to reach its target organ in the periphery.
question: Which of the following correctly characterizes preganglionic and postganglionic fiber lengths in the autonomic nervous system?

options.text: Parasympathetic: long postganglionic, short preganglionic fibers
Sympathetic: long postganglionic, short preganglionic fibers
Sympathetic: short postganglionic, long preganglionic fibers
Parasympathetic: long postganglionic and long preganglionic fibers
Somatic motor system: long postganglionic fibers arising from chain ganglia

explanation_correct: In the sympathetic division, preganglionic neurons are short (cell bodies in the spinal cord, ganglia nearby in the sympathetic chain) and postganglionic neurons are long, traveling out to distant targets such as vascular smooth muscle. This is the mirror image of the parasympathetic division, in which preganglionic neurons are long (brainstem nuclei or sacral cord) and postganglionic neurons are short (ganglia near the effector organ).

explanation_incorrect.A: This reverses the parasympathetic pattern; parasympathetic ganglia sit near or within the target organs, so postganglionic fibers are short and preganglionic fibers are long.
explanation_incorrect.C: This describes the parasympathetic division, not the sympathetic division.
explanation_incorrect.D: Parasympathetic preganglionic fibers are indeed long, but postganglionic fibers are short because ganglia lie close to the effector.
explanation_incorrect.E: The somatic motor system has no ganglia at all; a single neuron runs from the CNS directly to skeletal muscle.

educationalObjective: Contrast sympathetic (short pre, long postganglionic) with parasympathetic (long pre, short postganglionic) fiber lengths.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A medical student is asked to compare the somatic motor (voluntary) nervous system with the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions when reviewing an autonomic drugs lecture.
question: Which of the following features is unique to the somatic motor pathway?

options.text: It uses a two-neuron chain with a peripheral ganglion between the CNS and the effector
Its postganglionic fibers release norepinephrine onto adrenergic receptors
It innervates smooth muscle, gland cells, and cardiac muscle
Its effector receptors are muscarinic G-protein-coupled receptors
A single neuron runs from the CNS to skeletal muscle without synapsing in a ganglion

explanation_correct: The somatic motor pathway consists of a single voluntary motor neuron that travels from the spinal cord (or brainstem) directly to the neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle, releasing acetylcholine onto nicotinic (NM) receptors. There is no ganglion and no second neuron, unlike both autonomic divisions, which use a two-neuron preganglionic-postganglionic chain.

explanation_incorrect.A: A two-neuron chain with an intervening ganglion describes the autonomic (sympathetic and parasympathetic) pathways, not the somatic system.
explanation_incorrect.B: Norepinephrine release is characteristic of postganglionic sympathetic fibers; somatic neurons release acetylcholine.
explanation_incorrect.C: Smooth muscle, gland cells, and cardiac muscle are autonomic targets; somatic motor neurons innervate only skeletal muscle.
explanation_incorrect.D: Muscarinic receptors mediate parasympathetic (and cholinergic sympathetic sweat gland) effects; the neuromuscular junction uses nicotinic (NM) receptors.

educationalObjective: Distinguish the single-neuron somatic pathway (ACh on NM receptors at the neuromuscular junction) from the two-neuron autonomic pathways.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 50-year-old man participates in a physiology experiment in which he receives an investigational agent that selectively blocks nicotinic receptors in autonomic ganglia and the adrenal medulla (NN) but does not affect nicotinic receptors at the neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle (NM).
question: Which of the following functions would be expected to remain intact after administration of this agent?

options.text: Catecholamine release from the adrenal medulla
Parasympathetic output to the heart via the vagus nerve
Sympathetic output to vascular smooth muscle
Voluntary movement of skeletal muscle
Sympathetic-mediated sweating

explanation_correct: Voluntary skeletal muscle contraction depends on the somatic pathway, whose nicotinic receptors (NM) at the neuromuscular junction are unaffected by an NN-selective blocker. In contrast, all ganglionic transmission in both sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions, as well as preganglionic stimulation of the adrenal medulla, runs through NN receptors and would be blocked. Sweating, although cholinergic at its effector, still requires a preganglionic ganglionic synapse and is therefore also interrupted.

explanation_incorrect.A: The adrenal medulla is directly innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers acting on NN receptors, so catecholamine release would be blocked.
explanation_incorrect.B: Vagal (parasympathetic) output to the heart requires a preganglionic-postganglionic synapse at an NN receptor in a ganglion, so it would be blocked.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sympathetic output to vascular smooth muscle requires ganglionic NN transmission before the postganglionic neuron, so it would be blocked.
explanation_incorrect.E: Although the sweat gland effector synapse is muscarinic, the pathway first passes through an NN synapse in the sympathetic chain, which is blocked.

educationalObjective: Understand that NN receptors mediate all autonomic ganglionic transmission and adrenal medulla activation, while NM receptors mediate skeletal muscle contraction.
